note: Authored Study Room quiz items. Code items are validated by execution.

items.code: console.log('3' + 4, '3' * 4)
items.explanation: + with a string concatenates; * converts both operands to numbers.

items.code: console.log(0.1 + 0.2 === 0.3, Math.round(2.5), 7 % -3)
items.explanation: 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004; Math.round rounds .5 up; % takes the sign of the dividend.

items.prompt: total(a, b) receives two numeric strings such as '3' and '4' and must return their numeric sum. Fix it.
items.explanation: + concatenates strings; convert with Number() first.

items.code: console.log(0 == '', 0 === '', null == undefined)
items.explanation: == coerces '' to 0 and treats null and undefined as equal; === never coerces.

items.code:
const n = 0;
console.log(n || 5, n ?? 5)
items.explanation: || replaces any falsy value; ?? replaces only null and undefined.

items.prompt: withDefault(value) should return value unless it is null, in which case return 10. Zero is a valid value. Fix it.
items.explanation: || treats 0 as missing; ?? only replaces null or undefined.
for...in iterates keys (as strings); for...of iterates values.
let creates a new binding per iteration, so each closure keeps its own i.

items.prompt: sumTo(n) should return 1 + 2 + ... + n. It is off by one. Fix it.
items.explanation: Use <= so the loop includes n.

items.code:
function f(a, b = a * 2) { return a + b; }
console.log(f(1), f(1, 0), f(1, undefined))
items.explanation: Defaults apply when the argument is missing or undefined, but not for 0.
Automatic semicolon insertion ends the return statement at the line break.

items.prompt: distance(a, b) must return a non-negative distance. Fix it.
items.explanation: Math.abs makes the result independent of argument order.

items.code: console.log('héllo'.length, '😀'.length, [...'😀'].length)
items.explanation: length counts UTF-16 code units; the emoji is two units but one code point when spread.
Strings are immutable; the index assignment is ignored (outside strict mode).

items.prompt: countVowels(text) should count a, e, i, o, u. It reads past the end and miscounts. Fix it.
items.explanation: Indices run 0 through length - 1.

items.code: console.log([10, 9, 1].sort().join(','))
items.explanation: Default sort compares strings, so '10' sorts before '9'. Pass (a, b) => a - b for numbers.
b is the same array as a; the spread made c a separate copy.

items.prompt: sortedCopy(values) should return a new array of numbers sorted ascending without changing values. Fix it.
items.explanation: Copy before sorting and pass a numeric comparator.
Object keys are strings, so 1 and '1' collide. Map keeps the number and the string apart.
get on a missing key returns undefined; ?? supplied 0 for the first count.

items.prompt: countTarget(words, target) builds a frequency Map. Counts come out as NaN. Fix it.
items.explanation: undefined + 1 is NaN; default the missing count to 0.

items.code:
const s = new Set([1, 1, '1', {}, {}]);
console.log(s.size)
items.explanation: 1 is stored once, '1' is a different value, and each {} literal is a distinct object: 4 entries.

items.code:
const seen = new Set();
console.log(seen.add(2).has(2), seen.has('2'))
items.explanation: add returns the set, so has can be chained; '2' is a different value from 2.

items.prompt: uniqueCount(values) should return the number of distinct numbers. It returns the full length. Fix it.
items.explanation: The set's size is the distinct count.
this depends on how a function is called; call({ n: 5 }) binds this explicitly and returns 5, a number.
Spread copies one level; both objects still share the tags array.

items.prompt: finalBalance(initial, changes) must start each call from initial. A module-level account leaks state between calls. Fix it.
items.explanation: Create the account inside the call so each call has its own state.

items.code:
const xs = [1, 2];
console.log(xs[5], xs.at(-1))
items.explanation: Out-of-range reads return undefined rather than throwing; at(-1) reads from the end.

items.code: console.log(Number('12a'), parseInt('12a', 10), Number(''))
items.explanation: Number rejects trailing junk, parseInt stops at it, and Number('') is 0.

items.prompt: safeAt(values, index, fallback) must return fallback for any invalid index. It returns undefined. Fix it.
items.explanation: Check both ends of the valid range before reading.

items.code:
const f = (xs) => xs.length === 0 ? 0 : xs[0] + f(xs.slice(1));
console.log(f([1, 2, 3, 4]))
items.explanation: f sums the array recursively: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10.

items.code:
function depth(n) { return n <= 0 ? 0 : 1 + depth(n - 2); }
console.log(depth(5), depth(4))
items.explanation: 5 -> 3 -> 1 -> -1 takes three steps; 4 -> 2 -> 0 takes two.

items.prompt: digitSum(n) should sum the decimal digits of n recursively. It never terminates properly because n / 10 is not an integer. Fix it.
items.explanation: JavaScript / is floating point; floor it to drop the last digit.

items.prompt: What is the time complexity of hasDup for n elements?
items.explanation: indexOf scans the array for each element, so the work is quadratic. A Set makes it O(n).
shift removes from the front (and re-indexes, which is O(n) for large arrays).

items.prompt: hasPair(values, target) must not pair an element with itself. Fix it.
items.explanation: Check before adding so the set only contains earlier elements.
